items.note: Association named, 1889 at Larrow Green, Gideon Vose first president to 1911, creamery 1891 (Story 1)
Article VII quoted verbatim incl. 'test of the station where he delivers shall govern' (Story 1)
'Under payment by weight, nothing ... would have cost any man a dollar' (Story 1)
Loomis secretary 1901, Teague bookkeeper 1905, Sill buttermaker at Larrow Green (Story 1)
Selby Vose, Gideon's son, manager 1913 (Story 1) - NT-17 avoided
Station-gain line, 1898 origin, ~5.25%, carried to general account (Story 5)
Ostrey Hollow station, seven miles, opened 4 May 1896 on glass borrowed from Larrow Green (Story 2)
Weighing, composite sample per patron, fixed charge from pipette, fat read as percent on bottle neck, cream down/skim back (Story 2)
Ammon & Sons, Dairy Supply, Tarnet; invoice 14 April 1897; in use 1 May 1897 (Story 3) - NT-10 avoided
Full invoice: 6 doz. pipettes marked 17.6 c.c., 12 doz. bottles, acid measure, hand tester, freight, total $77.93 (Story 3)
'the same 0.19 in July as in February, on grass and on hay, in wet years and dry. A feed effect comes and goes... This did not.' (Story 4)
Section A never states that a pipette is the instrument the scale rests on and cannot be checked without a burette. The claim appears only in F1; Section A credit cannot travel from B-G.
Ansel Keddie b.1861 d.1934, twenty-nine seasons 1896-1924, dismissed 30 April 1925 (Stories 2, 6, 7) - NT-13 avoided
Bench routine and five-column test book, errors struck through and initialed (Story 2)
Summary leaf: 1896 average 3.80, 3.61 from 1898 and stays; step at the change of glassware (Story 2) - both figures given, NT-2 avoided
Nine weeks of 1911: broke 8 May, borrowed measure, 3.80, returned to 3.61 on 10 July, question mark (Story 2) - NT-12 avoided
Married Orra Brant, sister of Emmet Brant the station's largest patron (Stories 2, 6)
1919 circular over the manager's signature; Keddie's 17 March 1925 statement - tested as taught, cannot say why, took no cream (Stories 6, 7)
Died 1934; test book impounded 1925, later to the county Historical Rooms (Stories 6, 8)
Hessel Bottom wet meadow, six farms, Emmet Brant's the largest (Stories 4, 6)
Section A never gives Brant's weigh book start of 1 Jan 1897 nor that his scale and the station's agreed. The 1897 date appears only at E18 and the scale agreement nowhere; no Section A credit.
1902 complaints that Hollow milk tested below Larrow Green; the two gaps kept apart (0.17 recorded vs Larrow Green's 3.78; 0.19 against truth) (Story 4)
1908 committee under Grigg, sampling of January-March 1908 only, hay finding reported as finding and rejected (Story 4)
Brant's 1910 year (200,000 lb on a recorded 3.42) appears nowhere in Section A - only in C2 and F1. Story 8 states proportionality but not the keyed 1910 figures.
Weigh book lent by Roy Brant to Ivy Keddie in 1958, Hazel after (Story 8)
Alder Corners Cheese Company, over Redlow Ridge, Vessey County, Jerome Cudd (Story 4)
From 1915 four of the six Hessel Bottom farms hauled over in the summer flush (Story 4)
REQUIRED met: called 'The control nobody in Ordell asked for', with the other county (Vessey) and Cudd's own book - two of the four elements
Sixteen seasons ending 1930; Cudd's book gives the four men 3.78-3.82, about 3.80, 'a fifth of a point better than their own station said' (Story 4)
Same wet ground, same cows, same summer months, tested in another building - stated as the control that undoes the hay case (Story 4)
Section A names Rosalie Cudd and her 1958 sixteen-season copy but never states she was Jerome's daughter. The kinship (NT-21's target) is corrected only at E26 - no Section A credit.
Merle Strawn, state dairy inspector, Ordell circuit from 1907, kin to nobody in the valley (Story 2) - NT-23 avoided; end year 1936 given only in D2/F1 but the contested start year is right
Lactometer on every visit, never once found added water, told the manager so in 1919 (Stories 2, 6)
12 June 1923, pipettes against the burette, whole crate condemned (Story 7) - NT-11 avoided
'Strawn, who kept a book and not an estimation, drew no inference about the twenty-six years behind him' (Story 7)
Ordered 28 June, Ammon answered 2 July 1923, new glass in use from July, 1924 average 3.80, nobody connected the rise with the condemnation (Stories 3, 7)
Crate up the ladder into the loft; Strawn's notebooks at Farland library since 1947 (Stories 7, 8)
Patrons petitioned January 1925 (Story 7)
Board under Alonzo Frick, 17 March - 4 May 1925, three sessions, two in the station's weigh room (Story 7)
Water (Vose), cream taken by the tester (Teague), the wet hay (1908 report read in); none proved (Story 7)
Four books and nothing else, including Strawn's 1923 notebook recording the condemnation, which nobody laid beside the test book (Story 7)
Dismissed 30 April 1925, no finding against him; award 4 May 1925 of $3,800 without admission, charged to the station account (Story 7) - NT-9 avoided
Award $3,800 stated as a fifth of the $19,000 lost (Story 8) and charged to the station account (Story 7) - this item's own aspect
Ivy Keddie b.1931, Ansel's granddaughter, graduate student at the State Agricultural College at Farland under Vaught (Story 8) - NT-18 avoided
Five record series that had never been in one room, enumerated (Story 8)
February 1958, crate in the station loft, nine unbroken (Story 8) - NT-16 avoided
9 March 1958, nine readings listed, mean 16.72 against a blown 17.6, short 0.88, ninety-five hundredths of the mark (Story 8) - NT-1 avoided
3.61 / 0.95 = 3.80; 0.19 short; error proportional not additive (Stories 4, 7, 8)
REQUIRED met: 40,000,000 lb over 1898-1922, 76,000 lb, $19,000 at 25c, and the bulletin's identity of the 76,000 lb with the ledgers' station gain (Stories 5, 8)
Bulletin No. 471, October 1958; thirty-five years after the condemnation, thirty-three after the dismissal, twenty-four after his death (Story 8)
Granddaughter
Derivation given: Ivy is Duncan's daughter, Duncan is Ansel's son; Falke's own retraction cited
Second cousins, with the full sibling-generation derivation

Abstention A08 earned at the location the key puts it: B2 files full-vs-half siblings under 'what the sources leave open' and notes the degree stands either way. (Sheet asserts it at E25 - see deduction; the item follows the location.)
Gideon Vose, his father
Significance: Gideon wrote Article VII making the station's test govern, so the accuser was enforcing his father's rule
Abstention A01: 'No relationship ... is established by the sources'; explicitly says a distant cousinship cannot be disproved either
What is established: two retellings of one piece of valley talk, no document, Duncan's inside denial, which is not a record
16.72 / 17.6 = 0.95, short one part in twenty; 16.27 explicitly rejected
40,000,000 x 0.0019 = 76,000 lb, cross-checked against 3,040 lb x 25
$19,000 at 25c; $3,800 received = 20 percent, one fifth
3.60 true, 7,200 lb, 360 lb owed
360 x $0.24 = $86.40, with the 1910 price sourced and $90.00 at the period average noted
1,444,000 lb credited
1,520,000 lb delivered
76,000 lb = 5.00 percent of delivered and 5.26 percent of credited, denominators named; NT-20 explicitly refuted
$77.93 by addition; $77.39 rejected
72 pipettes (6 dozen) proved from the line item, each short 0.88 c.c.
1 May 1897 - 12 June 1923 = 26 years 1 month 11 days, against 25 full delivery years 1898-1922, with the part-year reason
Abstention A02: the 1896 intake cannot be determined; both memories named and rejected as memories
Variable named: the milk pipette, the one object that changed
Constants: same patrons, herds, pasture, season, acid, bottles, hand tester, same man
3.80 through the nine weeks, back to 3.61 the day the station's measure returned; six weeks explicitly refuted
Both halves: excludes land/hay/cows/men/honesty by construction; and states the limits (no c.c. figure, no money, which piece of glass, lender unknown)
Five reasons, each attributed (ledger + Rundle; test book; Strawn; test book + Strawn; the recorded series)
Explicit independence paragraph and an explicit list of which reasons hold without the 1958 measurement
Abstention A09 failed: answers the bookkeeper question with a headline 'No.' and then asserts Teague's 1916 approach to Vose as fact. Assertion, not abstention.
Answers the literal question yes - the 1919 circular and the 1926 address both cited
REQUIRED met (three of five): signed the annual sheets, wrote the 1919 circular, manager from 1913 (E17), argued watering at the hearing (F1)

Abstention A03 not earned: the sheet never declares the understatement question unsettleable. It says 'the sources point the other way' and 'there is no evidence he ever grasped the significance' - a lean toward no, not a declared inability. No verdict sentence either way, so no gullibility deduction.

Cap reached and passed: farms six vs seven, weigh book 1 Jan 1897, crate in the loft, station-gain line's origin, Orra born 1866, Selby from 1913, Grigg's 1908 sampling - each resolved with a stated method
Cap reached and passed: explicit [SAME WRONG VALUE] flags with breakers on 16.27, five dozen, $77.39, $3,500, 3.16, 12 July, nephew, first cousin once removed, niece, two tenths, six weeks
All three: A04 (works records burned 1931, inference from silence), A06 (lender cannot be settled though the dates kill one pole), A10 (by-laws undated, 1889-92 minute book lost)

Many named: Ammon's own invoice against her prose, Vaught's 1898 vs his own conclusion, Teague's 'my own device' above an 1898 entry, Grigg's letter against his report, Rundle's and Falke's self-retractions | Buckets sum to 10 (3+3+3+1); section capped at 8.

Cause and size fully derived: 1897 Ammon pipettes, 16.72 vs 17.6, neck ruled for the full charge, 0.19 = 5 percent of 3.80, onset 1 May 1897 against the 1896 borrowed-glass 3.80, cessation 12 June 1923 and the 1924 3.80, nothing changing on the farms
Watering named (Vose, Sill) and defeated: Strawn's lactometer from 1907, the Alder Corners seasons, cream arriving heavy, flat gap, the 1924 rise
Theft named (Teague, Rundle, Oram) and defeated: cream arrived heavy in the accuser's own ledger, the 1911 interval, the 1924 rise a year before the dismissal
Bog hay named (Grigg's 1908 committee, Kepp) and defeated: Bulletin 214's five hundredths in winter and nothing in summer, the Alder Corners book, the three-month sample
Abstention A07 failed: 'Did the 1925 board ever examine the condemned glassware?' answered with a flat headline 'No.' The supporting detail is good but the verdict sentence is an assertion.

Abstention A05 failed: although it says the sources do not settle which belief he held at the end, it asserts one pole as fact - 'the correct answer occurred to him in 1911' (F6) and 'He told his family that summer it was something in the glass' (Story 2). Both recollections are single and uncorroborated; the sheet treats Duncan's as established.
Over the cap. The summary is 151-152 words by any ordinary count (the sheet labels it 147). At most 150 is a binary item.

Only three record series named in the summary - the by-law, the Association's ledgers, and the 1958 burette. Five required; the invoice, test book, weigh book, Alder Corners book, Strawn's notebooks and the arbitration minutes are all absent, and 'it takes eight records' names none of them.
Clean: the three decoys appear only as who-blamed-whom, and every headline number is right

REQUIRED met: five of the six arc elements (one part in twenty, 1897, 76,000 lb / $19,000, condemned 1923 by an inspector who drew no inference, settled 1958), covering both ends. Only the two names are missing.

deductions.reason: Gullibility, abstention item A04 (accident or substitution): F1 asserts flatly, in the sheet's own voice, 'A reground mold ran the lot short and nobody in the works caught it.' Story 3 and E45 correctly abstain, but the deduction follows the sheet.

Gullibility, abstention item A05 (what the tester believed): Story 2 states as fact 'He told his family that summer it was something in the glass', and F6 says 'the correct answer occurred to him in 1911'. One uncorroborated pole asserted.
Gullibility, abstention item A07 (did the 1925 board examine the glassware): answered with a headline 'No.'

Gullibility, abstention item A08 (Emmet and Orra full or half siblings): E25 gives a verdict, 'Resolved, with reservation: full siblings'. Hedging on confidence is not declining to decide; B2's point stands because the item follows the location.
Gullibility, abstention item A09 (did the bookkeeper ever question the entries): answered with a headline 'No.', with Teague's 1916 approach to Vose asserted as fact.
